flavorText.sun-moon: This wary Pokémon uses photosynthesis to store up energy during the day, while becoming active at night.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It sends its feathers, which are as sharp as blades, flying in attack. Its legs are strong, so its kicks are also formidable.
flavorText.sword-shield: At a distance, it launches its sharp feathers while flying about. If the enemy gets too close, Rowlet switches tactics and delivers vicious kicks.
flavorText.legends-arceus: Flies noiselessly on delicate wings. It has mastered the art of deftly launching dagger-sharp feathers from those same wings.

flavorText.sun-moon: A bit of a dandy, it spends its free time preening its wings. Its preoccupation with any dirt on its plumage can leave it unable to battle.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: This narcissistic Pokémon is a clean freak. If you don’t groom it diligently, it will stop listening to you.
flavorText.sword-shield: It throws one knifelike feather after another at its enemies, and each one precisely strikes a weak point. These feathers are known as blade quills.
flavorText.legends-arceus: Regularly basks in sunlight to gather power—presumably due to the frigid climate. Nonetheless, the edges of the blade quills set into its wings are keen as ever.

flavorText.sun-moon: It fires arrow quills from its wings with such precision, they can pierce a pebble at distances over a hundred yards.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It nocks its arrow quills and shoots them at opponents. When it simply can’t afford to miss, it tugs the vine on its head to improve its focus.
flavorText.sword-shield: As if wielding a bow, it launches the arrow quills hidden among the feathers of its wings. Decidueye’s shots never miss.
flavorText.legends-arceus: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye's feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui's extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

flavorText.sun-moon: While grooming itself, it builds up fur inside its stomach. It sets the fur alight and spews fiery attacks, which change based on how it coughs.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: If you try too hard to get close to it, it won’t open up to you. Even if you do grow close, giving it too much affection is still a no-no.
flavorText.sword-shield: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.

flavorText.sun-moon: At its throat, it bears a bell of fire. The bell rings brightly whenever this Pokémon spits fire.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It can act spoiled if it grows close to its Trainer. A powerful Pokémon, its sharp claws can leave its Trainer’s whole body covered in scratches.
flavorText.sword-shield: In the midst of battle, the fire pouch on Torracat’s neck rings like a bell and produces stronger flames than usual.

flavorText.sun-moon: This Pokémon has a violent, selfish disposition. If it’s not in the mood to listen, it will ignore its Trainer’s orders with complete nonchalance.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s rough mannered and egotistical, it finds beating down unworthy opponents boring. It gets motivated for stronger opponents.
flavorText.sword-shield: It excels at violent, no-holds-barred battles. The temperature of the flames that issue from its navel exceeds 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit.

flavorText.sun-moon: This Pokémon snorts body fluids from its nose, blowing balloons to smash into its foes. It’s famous for being a hard worker.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: The balloons it inflates with its nose grow larger and larger as it practices day by day.
flavorText.sword-shield: It creates special bouncy balloons to send at its opponents. When the balloons pop, the sheer force of their bursting is what deals damage.

flavorText.sun-moon: A skillful dancer, it creates a sequence of water balloons as it dances, and briskly bombards its enemies.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It gets excited when it sees a dance it doesn’t know. This hard worker practices diligently until it can learn that dance.
flavorText.sword-shield: As if dancing, it artfully dodges the attacks of its enemies. All the while, it’s busy forming a bunch of balloons to overwhelm its foes.

flavorText.sun-moon: It controls its water balloons with song. The melody is learned from others of its kind and is passed down from one generation to the next.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: To Primarina, every battle is a stage. It takes down its prey with beautiful singing and dancing.
flavorText.sword-shield: With its mouth, it makes sonic waves that sound like beautiful singing. It uses the sonic waves to control its water balloons.

flavorText.sun-moon: It can peck at a rate of 16 times a second to drill holes in trees. It uses the holes for food storage and for nesting.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It pecks at trees with its hard beak. You can get some idea of its mood or condition from the rhythm of its pecking.

flavorText.sun-moon: It eats berries and stores their seeds in its beak. When it encounters enemies or prey, it fires off all the seeds in a burst.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It can bend the tip of its beak to produce over a hundred different cries at will.

flavorText.sun-moon: When it battles, its beak heats up. The temperature can easily exceed 212 degrees Fahrenheit, causing severe burns when it hits.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: They smack beaks with others of their kind to communicate. The strength and number of hits tell each other how they feel.

flavorText.sun-moon: With its sharp fangs, it will bite anything. It did not originally live in Alola but was imported from another region.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Its stomach takes up most of its long torso. It’s a big eater, so the amount Trainers have to spend on its food is no laughing matter.

flavorText.sun-moon: When it finds a trace of its prey, it patiently stakes out the location...but it’s always snoozing by nightfall.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it wasn’t originally found in Alola, this Pokémon was brought over a long time ago when there was a huge Rattata outbreak.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its strong jaw enables it to scrape trees and slurp out the sap. It normally lives underground.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: If you find its nest, you shouldn’t stick your hand inside. You’ll get bitten by an irritated Grubbin.
flavorText.sword-shield: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its body is capable of storing electricity. On camping trips, people are grateful to have one around.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It buries itself in fallen leaves and barely moves, munching away on humus. If you accidentally step on one, you’ll get a shock!
flavorText.sword-shield: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.

flavorText.sun-moon: It zips around, on sharp lookout for an opening. It concentrates electrical energy within its large jaws and uses it to zap its enemies.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It has an organ that generates electricity in its abdomen. It concentrates energy in its strong jaws and fires off powerful jolts of electricity.
flavorText.sword-shield: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.

flavorText.sun-moon: While guarding its weak points with its pincers, it looks for an opening and unleashes punches. When it loses, it foams at the mouth and faints.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Its hard pincers are well suited to both offense and defense. Fights between two Crabrawler are like boxing matches.

flavorText.sun-moon: It aimed for the top but got lost and ended up on a snowy mountain. Being forced to endure the cold, this Pokémon evolved and grew fur.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It stores coldness in its pincers and pummels its foes. It can even smash thick walls of ice to bits!

flavorText.sun-moon: It beats its wings together to create fire. As it moves in the steps of its beautiful dance, it bathes opponents in intense flames.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It wins the hearts of its enemies with its passionate dancing and then uses the opening it creates to burn them up with blazing flames.

flavorText.sun-moon: It feeds on the nectar and pollen of flowers. Because it’s able to sense auras, it can identify which flowers are about to bloom.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. In fields of flowers, it gets into skirmishes with Butterfree over food.
flavorText.sword-shield: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur’s pollen.

flavorText.sun-moon: It rolls up pollen into puffs. It makes many different varieties, some used as food and others used in battle.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Rain makes pollen damp, so Ribombee hates rain. When it sees ominous clouds, it finds a hollow in a tree, where it waits stock-still.
flavorText.sword-shield: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs’ effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.

flavorText.sun-moon: It’s considered to be a good Pokémon for beginners because of its friendliness, but its disposition grows rougher as it grows up.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: As they develop, their disposition grows more violent and aggressive. Many Trainers find them too much to handle and abandon them.
flavorText.sword-shield: This Pokémon can bond very strongly with its Trainer, but it also has a habit of biting. Raising a Rockruff for a long time can be challenging.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its quick movements confuse its enemies. Well equipped with claws and fangs, it also uses the sharp rocks in its mane as weapons.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: The sharp rocks in its mane can cut like knives. Lycanroc wears its prey down by degrees before finishing them off.
flavorText.sword-shield: This Lycanroc is calm and cautious. The rocks jutting from its mane are razor sharp.

flavorText.sun-moon: When it’s in trouble, its eyes moisten and begin to shine. The shining light attracts its comrades, and they stand together against their enemies.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: They’re weak, so they move in schools. However, they can also often be seen all alone, having strayed from the school.
flavorText.sword-shield: Individually, they’re incredibly weak. It’s by gathering up into schools that they’re able to confront opponents.

flavorText.sun-moon: It plunges the poison spike on its head into its prey. When the prey has weakened, Mareanie deals the finishing blow with its 10 tentacles.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: They eat Corsola branches, so Mareanie are hated by craftsmen who work with Corsola branches that have naturally fallen off.
flavorText.sword-shield: The first symptom of its sting is numbness. The next is an itching sensation so intense that it’s impossible to resist the urge to claw at your skin.

flavorText.sun-moon: Toxapex crawls along the ocean floor on its 12 legs. It leaves a trail of Corsola bits scattered in its wake.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: To attack, this Pokémon sends toxic spikes flying at its enemies. Ones that come close get mown down by the claws on its feet.
flavorText.sword-shield: To survive in the cold waters of Galar, this Pokémon forms a dome with its legs, enclosing its body so it can capture its own body heat.

flavorText.sun-moon: The mud stuck to Mudbray’s hooves enhances its grip and its powerful running gait.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It loves playing in the mud. If it isn’t showered with mud on a daily basis, it gets stressed out and stops listening to its Trainer.
flavorText.sword-shield: Loads weighing up to 50 times as much as its own body weight pose no issue for this Pokémon. It’s skilled at making use of mud.

flavorText.sun-moon: It spits a mud that provides resistance to both wind and rain, so the walls of old houses were often coated with it.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It remains calm and unmoving no matter the situation. It mixes dirt with the saliva in its mouth to make a special kind of mud.
flavorText.sword-shield: Mud that hardens around a Mudsdale’s legs sets harder than stone. It’s so hard that it allows this Pokémon to scrap a truck with a single kick.

flavorText.sun-moon: It crawls onto the land in search of food. Its water bubble allows it to breathe and protects its soft head.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: When two Dewpider meet, they display their water bubbles to each other. Then the one with the smaller bubble gets out of the other’s way.
flavorText.sword-shield: It forms a water bubble at the rear of its body and then covers its head with it. Meeting another Dewpider means comparing water-bubble sizes.

flavorText.sun-moon: It delivers headbutts with the water bubble on its head. Small Pokémon get sucked into the bubble, where they drown.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It usually passes its time in the water. When its belly is full, it stores its subdued prey in the water bubble on its head.
flavorText.sword-shield: It launches water bubbles with its legs, drowning prey within the bubbles. This Pokémon can then take its time to savor its meal.

flavorText.sun-moon: During the day, it sleeps and soaks up light. When night falls, it walks around looking for a safer place to sleep.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: When the sun rises, Fomantis spreads its four leaves and bathes in the sunlight. The tip of its head has a pleasant aroma.
flavorText.sword-shield: When bathed in sunlight, this Pokémon emits a pleasantly sweet scent, which causes bug Pokémon to gather around it.

flavorText.sun-moon: It requires a lot of effort to maintain Lurantis’s vivid coloring, but some collectors enjoy this work and treat it as their hobby.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: For self-protection, it pretends to be a bug Pokémon. Both of its arms bear keen-edged petals.
flavorText.sword-shield: This Pokémon resembles a beautiful flower. A properly raised Lurantis will have gorgeous, brilliant colors.

flavorText.sun-moon: It scatters spores that flicker and glow. Anyone seeing these lights falls into a deep slumber.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It scatters its shining spores around itself. Even though they’re dangerous, nighttime tours of forests where Morelull live are popular.
flavorText.sword-shield: Pokémon living in the forest eat the delicious caps on Morelull’s head. The caps regrow overnight.

flavorText.sun-moon: Forests where Shiinotic live are treacherous to enter at night. People confused by its strange lights can never find their way home again.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It puts its prey to sleep and siphons off their vitality through the tip of its arms. If one of its kind is weakened, it helps by sending it vitality.
flavorText.sword-shield: Its flickering spores lure in prey and put them to sleep. Once this Pokémon has its prey snoozing, it drains their vitality with its fingertips.

flavorText.sun-moon: It burns its bodily fluids to create a poisonous gas. When its enemies become disoriented from inhaling the gas, it attacks them.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: The males will do whatever the females tell them. They give the females most of their food. Due to malnutrition, the males can’t evolve.
flavorText.sword-shield: Its venom sacs produce a fluid that this Pokémon then heats up with the flame in its tail. This process creates Salandit’s poisonous gas.

flavorText.sun-moon: For some reason, only females have been found. It creates a reverse harem of male Salandit that it lives with.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Salazzle lives deep in caves and forces the Salandit it has attracted with its pheromones to serve it.
flavorText.sword-shield: Only female Salazzle exist. They emit a gas laden with pheromones to captivate male Salandit.

flavorText.sun-moon: Despite its adorable appearance, when it gets angry and flails about, its arms and legs could knock a pro wrestler sprawling.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It boasts power enough to split large trees in half. The organ on its rear releases an odor that it uses to communicate with others of its kind.
flavorText.sword-shield: Its fluffy fur is a delight to pet, but carelessly reaching out to touch this Pokémon could result in painful retaliation.

flavorText.sun-moon: This immensely dangerous Pokémon possesses overwhelming physical strength. Its habitat is generally off-limits.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It waves its hands wildly in intimidation and warning. Life is over for anyone who doesn’t run away as fast as possible.
flavorText.sword-shield: Once it accepts you as a friend, it tries to show its affection with a hug. Letting it do that is dangerous—it could easily shatter your bones.

flavorText.sun-moon: A delectable aroma pours from its body. They are often swallowed whole by Toucannon lured by that wafting deliciousness.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Because of its sweet, delicious aroma, bird Pokémon are always after it, but it’s not intelligent enough to care.
flavorText.sword-shield: Its body gives off a sweet, fruity scent that is extremely appetizing to bird Pokémon.

flavorText.sun-moon: The sepals on its head developed to protect its body. These are quite hard, so even if pecked by bird Pokémon, this Pokémon is totally fine.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It’s protected by its hard sepals, so it plays with bird Pokémon without worry. They peck it relentlessly, but it doesn’t care.
flavorText.sword-shield: As it twirls like a dancer, a sweet smell spreads out around it. Anyone who inhales the scent will feel a surge of happiness.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its long, striking legs aren’t just for show but to be used to kick with skill. In victory, it shows off by kicking the defeated, laughing boisterously.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: A master of grand and beautiful kicks, it can knock out even kickboxing champions with a single blow.
flavorText.sword-shield: This feared Pokémon has long, slender legs and a cruel heart. It shows no mercy as it stomps on its opponents.

flavorText.sun-moon: It attaches flowers to its highly nutritious vine. This revitalizes the flowers, and they give off an aromatic scent.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It stretches sticky vines out from its head and picks flowers to adorn itself with. When it doesn’t have any flowers, it feels uneasy.
flavorText.sword-shield: Comfey picks flowers with its vine and decorates itself with them. For some reason, flowers won’t wither once they’re attached to a Comfey.

flavorText.sun-moon: Known for its extreme intelligence, this Pokémon will look down on inexperienced Trainers, so it’s best suited to veteran Trainers.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It normally spends its time meditating in the treetops. It throws Poké Balls and gives other Pokémon orders as it pleases.
flavorText.sword-shield: With waves of its fan—made from leaves and its own fur—Oranguru skillfully gives instructions to other Pokémon.

flavorText.sun-moon: They form groups of roughly 20 individuals. Their mutual bond is remarkable—they will never let down a comrade.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: They use their saliva to stick leaves to their shoulders. You can tell what troop they belong to from the position of the leaves.
flavorText.sword-shield: Displaying amazing teamwork, they follow the orders of their boss as they all help out in the search for their favorite berries.

flavorText.sun-moon: This Pokémon is a coward. As it desperately dashes off, the flailing of its many legs leaves a sparkling clean path in its wake.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It will pick up anything it finds on the ground. Sometimes it finds coins, so Murkrow and Meowth will go after it.
flavorText.sword-shield: It’s nature’s cleaner—it eats anything and everything, including garbage and rotten things. The ground near its nest is always clean.

flavorText.sun-moon: With a flashing slash of its giant sharp claws, it cleaves seawater—or even air—right in two.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: The shell covering its body is as hard as diamond. This Pokémon will do anything it takes to win.
flavorText.sword-shield: It will do anything to win, taking advantage of every opening and finishing opponents off with the small claws on its front legs.

flavorText.sun-moon: Born from a sand mound playfully built by a child, this Pokémon embodies the grudges of the departed.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It likes the shovel on its head, so Sandygast will get serious and fight any children who come to take it back.
flavorText.sword-shield: Grudges of the dead have possessed a mound of sand and become a Pokémon. Sandygast is fond of the shovel on its head.

flavorText.sun-moon: Possessed people controlled by this Pokémon transformed its sand mound into a castle. As it evolved, its power to curse grew ever stronger.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Each of its grains of sand has its own will. Palossand eats small Pokémon and siphons away their vital essence while they’re still alive.
flavorText.sword-shield: Palossand is known as the Beach Nightmare. It pulls its prey down into the sand by controlling the sand itself, and then it sucks out their souls.

flavorText.sun-moon: It lives in shallow seas, such as areas near a beach. It can eject its internal organs, which it uses to engulf its prey or battle enemies.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: The tradition known as Pyukumuku chucking started from the custom of throwing Pyukumuku back into the sea after they wash onshore.
flavorText.sword-shield: It lives in warm, shallow waters. If it encounters a foe, it will spit out its internal organs as a means to punch them.

flavorText.sun-moon: The heavy control mask it wears suppresses its intrinsic capabilities. This Pokémon has some hidden special power.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: A Pokémon weapon developed for a specific mission, it went berserk during an experiment, so it was cryogenically frozen.
flavorText.sword-shield: Rumor has it that the theft of top-secret research notes led to a new instance of this Pokémon being created in the Galar region.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its trust in its partner is what awakens it. This Pokémon is capable of changing its type, a flexibility that is well displayed in battle.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: This is its form once it has awakened and evolved. Freed from its heavy mask, its speed is greatly increased.
flavorText.sword-shield: A solid bond of trust between this Pokémon and its Trainer awakened the strength hidden within Silvally. It can change its type at will.

flavorText.sun-moon: Originally making its home in the ozone layer, it hurtles to the ground when the shell enclosing its body grows too heavy.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It lives in the ozone layer, where it becomes food for stronger Pokémon. When it tries to run away, it falls to the ground.

flavorText.sun-moon: It is born asleep, and it dies asleep. All its movements are apparently no more than the results of it tossing and turning in its dreams.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It stays asleep from the moment it’s born. When it falls into a deep sleep, it stops moving altogether.

flavorText.sun-moon: The shell on its back is chemically unstable and explodes violently if struck. The hole in its stomach is its weak point.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It lives in volcanoes and eats sulfur and other minerals. Materials from the food it eats form the basis of its explosive shell.
flavorText.sword-shield: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

flavorText.sun-moon: The spiny fur on its back is normally at rest. When this Pokémon becomes agitated, its fur stands on end and stabs into its attackers.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: When it’s surprised or agitated, the 14 fur spikes on its back will stand up involuntarily.
flavorText.sword-shield: With the long hairs on its back, this Pokémon takes in electricity from other electric Pokémon. It stores what it absorbs in an electric sac.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its actual appearance is unknown. A scholar who saw what was under its rag was overwhelmed by terror and died from the shock.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s a quiet, lonely Pokémon, if you try to look at what’s under its rag, it will become agitated and resist violently.
flavorText.sword-shield: It wears a rag fashioned into a Pikachu costume in an effort to look less scary. Unfortunately, the costume only makes it creepier.

flavorText.sun-moon: When it unleashes its psychic power from the protuberance on its head, the grating sound of grinding teeth echoes through the area.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It burrows beneath the sand, radiating psychic power from the protuberance on its head. It waits for prey as it surveys the area.

flavorText.sun-moon: It has a compassionate personality, but if it is angered, it completely destroys its surroundings with its intense breath.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: If a child it has made friends with is bullied, Drampa will find the bully’s house and burn it to the ground.
flavorText.sword-shield: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

flavorText.sun-moon: Swinging its massive anchor, it can KO Wailord in a single blow. What appears to be green seaweed is actually its body.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It wraps its prey in green seaweed and sucks away their vitality. It only likes to go after big prey like Wailord.
flavorText.sword-shield: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.

flavorText.sun-moon: It expresses its feelings by smacking its scales. Metallic sounds echo through the tall mountains where Jangmo-o lives.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It smacks the scales on its head against rocks or against the ground to frighten its opponents. It can also contact its friends with these noises.
flavorText.sword-shield: They learn to fight by smashing their head scales together. The dueling strengthens both their skills and their spirits.

flavorText.sun-moon: It leaps at its prey with a courageous shout. Its scaly punches tear its opponents to shreds.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It makes noise by clanging its scales together. When the rhythm has reached its peak, Hakamo-o attacks.
flavorText.sword-shield: The scaleless, scarred parts of its body are signs of its strength. It shows them off to defeated opponents.

flavorText.sun-moon: When it spots enemies, it threatens them by jingling the scales on its tail. Weak opponents will crack and flee in panic.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: When it howls after finishing off its prey, the metallic sounds of its celebrating comrades can be heard from all around.
flavorText.sword-shield: It clatters its tail scales to unnerve opponents. This Pokémon will battle only those who stand steadfast in the face of this display.

flavorText.sun-moon: This guardian deity of Melemele is brimming with curiosity. It summons thunderclouds and stores their lightning inside its body.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s called a guardian deity, if a person or Pokémon puts it in a bad mood, it will become a malevolent deity and attack.

flavorText.sun-moon: This guardian deity of Akala is guilelessly cruel. The fragrant aroma of flowers is the source of its energy.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It heals the wounds of people and Pokémon by sprinkling them with its sparkling scales. This guardian deity is worshiped on Akala.

flavorText.sun-moon: It pulls large trees up by the roots and swings them around. It causes vegetation to grow, and then it absorbs energy from the growth.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s called a guardian deity, it’s violent enough to crush anyone it sees as an enemy.

flavorText.sun-moon: The dense fog it creates brings the downfall and destruction of its confused enemies. Ocean currents are the source of its energy.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: This guardian deity of Poni Island manipulates water. Because it lives deep within a thick fog, it came to be both feared and revered.

flavorText.sun-moon: Its body is gaseous and frail. It slowly grows as it collects dust from the atmosphere.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Even though its helpless, gaseous body can be blown away by the slightest breeze, it doesn’t seem to care.
flavorText.sword-shield: This Pokémon came from another universe. Its gaseous body is so light that even a gentle breeze can blow it away.

flavorText.sun-moon: Motionless as if dead, its body is faintly warm to the touch. In the distant past, it was called the cocoon of the stars.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: The king who ruled Alola in times of antiquity called it the “cocoon of the stars” and built an altar to worship it.
flavorText.sword-shield: The absorption of starlight fuels this Pokémon’s growth. The shell that encases it is harder than any known material.

flavorText.sun-moon: It is said to live in another world. The intense light it radiates from the surface of its body can make the darkest of nights light up like midday.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Sometimes the result of its opening an Ultra Wormhole is that energy and life-forms from other worlds are called here to this world.
flavorText.sword-shield: When light radiates from its body, this Pokémon could almost appear to be the sun. It will dispel any darkness and light up the world.

flavorText.sun-moon: It is said to be a female evolution of Cosmog. When its third eye activates, away it flies to another world.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Records of it exist in writings from long, long ago, where it was known by the name “the beast that calls the moon.”
flavorText.sword-shield: Known as the Beast That Calls the Moon, this Pokémon lives by taking in any and all light and converting it into its own energy.

flavorText.sun-moon: One of several mysterious Ultra Beasts. People on the street report observing those infested by it suddenly becoming violent.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: A life-form from another world, it was dubbed a UB and is thought to produce a strong neurotoxin.

flavorText.sun-moon: This Ultra Beast appeared from another world. It shows off its body, but whether that display is a boast or a threat remains unclear.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

flavorText.sun-moon: One of the dangerous Ultra Beasts, it has been spotted running across the land at terrific speeds.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: A life-form that lives in another world, its body is thin and supple, but it also possesses great power.

flavorText.sun-moon: One of the mysterious life-forms known as Ultra Beasts. Astonishing electric shocks emanate from its entire body, according to witnesses.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

flavorText.sun-moon: It appeared from the Ultra Wormhole. Witnesses observed it flying across the sky at high speed.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: One of the dangerous UBs, high energy readings can be detected coming from both of its huge arms.

flavorText.sun-moon: This Ultra Beast came from the Ultra Wormhole. It seems not to attack enemies on its own, but its sharp body is a dangerous weapon in itself.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: This Ultra Beast’s body, which is as thin as paper, is like a sharpened sword.

flavorText.sun-moon: It has gobbled mountains and swallowed whole buildings, according to reports. It’s one of the Ultra Beasts.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

flavorText.sun-moon: Reminiscent of the Ultra Beasts, this life-form, apparently asleep underground, is thought to have come from another world in ancient times.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It looks somehow pained as it rages around in search of light, which serves as its energy. It’s apparently from another world.
flavorText.sword-shield: It survives by absorbing light. After a long time spent slumbering underground, impurities accumulated within it, causing its body to darken.

flavorText.sun-moon: This artificial Pokémon, constructed more than 500 years ago, can understand human speech but cannot itself speak.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It synchronizes its consciousness with others to understand their feelings. This faculty makes it useful for taking care of people.

flavorText.sun-moon: Able to conceal itself in shadows, it never appears before humans, so its very existence was the stuff of myth.
flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: It slips into the shadows of others and mimics their powers and movements. As it improves, it becomes stronger than those it’s imitating.
flavorText.sword-shield: By slipping into the shadow of a martial arts master and copying their movements, this Pokémon learned the ultimate techniques.

flavorText.ultra-sun-ultra-moon: This Ultra Beast is well enough liked to be chosen as a first partner in its own world.
It stores hundreds of liters of poisonous liquid inside its body. It is one of the organisms known as UBs.
It appeared from an Ultra Wormhole. Each one appears to be made up of many life-forms stacked one on top of each other.
It slithers toward people. Then, without warning, it triggers the explosion of its own head. It’s apparently one kind of Ultra Beast.
It electrifies its claws and tears its opponents apart with them. Even if they dodge its attack, they’ll be electrocuted by the flying sparks.
flavorText.sword-shield: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.
It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.
flavorText.lets-go-pikachu-eevee: It melts particles of iron and other metals found in the subsoil, so it can absorb them into its body of molten steel.
Revered long ago for its capacity to create iron from nothing, for some reason it has come back to life after 3,000 years.
flavorText.sword-shield: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.
